agreement_text: CREDIT AGREEMENT dated May 20, 2025, among Cedar Reach Field Services, LLC, as Borrower, its designated material domestic subsidiaries as Guarantors, the lenders party hereto, and Granite Field Bank, as Administrative Agent and Collateral Agent. 1. Facilities. The Lenders establish a $95,000,000 USD term loan facility and a $25,000,000 USD revolving facility. The term loan is funded on the Closing Date. Revolving loans may be borrowed, repaid and reborrowed until May 20, 2030. The revolver includes a $4,000,000 letter-of-credit sublimit and a $3,000,000 swingline sublimit. Borrowings must be at least $1,000,000 and in $100,000 increments. Proceeds may refinance existing indebtedness, fund equipment purchases, working capital and general corporate purposes, and finance permitted acquisitions. Each borrowing is subject to customary conditions, including that no default is continuing and the requested amount does not exceed availability. 2. Interest and Fees. SOFR loans bear one- or three-month Term SOFR, with a 1.00% floor, plus 4.25% per annum for term loans and 3.75% for revolving loans. Base-rate loans bear the base rate plus 3.25% for term loans or 2.75% for revolving loans. Interest is payable monthly in arrears. The Borrower pays a 0.50% annual fee on unused revolving commitments, payable monthly, and letter-of-credit fees at 3.75% per annum on the undrawn amount. During a continuing event of default, overdue amounts bear an additional 2.00% per annum. 3. Maturity and Repayment. The term loan matures May 20, 2031, and revolving loans and commitments mature May 20, 2030. Term principal amortizes quarterly at 2.50% per annum of original principal, with all remaining principal due at maturity. Voluntary prepayments are permitted without premium on one business day's notice, subject to accrued interest. The Borrower must prepay term loans with 100% of net proceeds from non-permitted debt and asset-sale proceeds exceeding $5,000,000 in a fiscal year, unless such sale proceeds are reinvested within 180 days. Net insurance and condemnation proceeds above $5,000,000 are subject to the same reinvestment period. 4. Financial Covenant. On the last day of each fiscal quarter, the Borrower must maintain a fixed-charge coverage ratio of at least 1.10:1.00, calculated as consolidated EBITDA less unfinanced capital expenditures, divided by consolidated fixed charges for the preceding four quarters. The first test is for the quarter ending September 30, 2025. If the Borrower fails the test, it may cure by contributing cash equity within 10 business days after delivery of the relevant compliance certificate; the contribution is included in EBITDA solely for covenant calculation. No more than two cures may be used in any four-quarter period, and no cure may be used in consecutive quarters. 5. Restrictive Covenants. The Borrower and restricted subsidiaries may not incur debt or liens, make investments or restricted payments, dispose of assets, merge, or enter affiliate transactions except as permitted. Permitted debt includes ordinary-course trade obligations and equipment-financing debt up to $12,000,000 outstanding; permitted liens include liens securing the facilities, statutory liens and liens on financed equipment. Investments in wholly owned guarantors and ordinary-course customer advances are permitted. Restricted payments are permitted only from available builder capacity when no default is continuing and pro forma fixed-charge coverage is at least 1.25:1.00. Asset sales must be for fair value; sales of equipment are permitted if replaced with functionally comparable property within 180 days. Mergers are permitted where the Borrower survives or a successor assumes the obligations and no default results. Affiliate transactions must be on fair terms, with exceptions for intercompany transactions and ordinary-course compensation. 6. Amendment and Waiver. By written amendment dated February 18, 2026, the Required Lenders waived the fixed-charge coverage covenant failure for the quarter ended December 31, 2025, after the Borrower reported a ratio of 1.06:1.00. The waiver is limited to that quarter, does not alter the 1.10:1.00 threshold for subsequent quarters and does not waive any other default. The amendment also permits the Borrower to defer the February 2026 scheduled term installment until March 31, 2026, without default, provided accrued interest is paid on that date. Other amendments and waivers require Required Lender consent, with each directly affected lender's consent required for reductions of principal or margin, extensions of scheduled payment dates or commitment increases. 7. Events of Default. Events include failure to pay principal when due or other amounts within three business days; breach of financial or specified negative covenants; other covenant breaches continuing 20 days after notice; materially false representations; cross-default on other debt exceeding $10,000,000 after applicable grace periods; bankruptcy or insolvency; final judgments exceeding $10,000,000 not paid, bonded or stayed within 45 days; and repudiation or invalidity of a material guarantee or security document. Upon a continuing event of default, the Agent may terminate commitments and accelerate all outstanding obligations, and the Collateral Agent may enforce its liens, subject to applicable law. 8. Reporting and Other Obligations. The Borrower must deliver monthly management accounts within 30 days after month end, quarterly and annual financial statements, quarterly covenant certificates, an annual operating plan, and prompt notice of defaults, litigation reasonably likely to result in liability above $5,000,000, and material casualty events. The Borrower must maintain insurance, preserve its existence and pay taxes before delinquency, subject to good-faith contests. It must reimburse reasonable documented Agent expenses and indemnify the secured parties for covered claims, excluding losses caused by gross negligence, bad faith or willful misconduct.

Monthly-pay floating-rate pricing includes a 1% SOFR floor, and term debt amortizes at 2.5% annually. A quarterly fixed-charge coverage covenant begins with the September 2025 quarter; limited equity cures are available. The agreement restricts debt, liens, investments, distributions, asset sales, mergers and affiliate dealings subject to specified baskets. A February 2026 amendment waived the December 2025 covenant failure and deferred one installment to March 31, 2026, without changing the ongoing covenant threshold. Defaults can lead to acceleration and lien enforcement. The Borrower also has detailed reporting, insurance, tax and expense obligations.
